text: {"distance_m": 2, "reasoning_short": "Rough estimate: about 2 m. 20/20 acuity (resolving about 1 arcmin) applies only to high-contrast detail. A small spot at only 5% contrast must look larger before it can be detected. By Ricco's law, contrast × area stays roughly constant for tiny targets. Under typical indoor (photopic) lighting, a 100% contrast spot is detectable at about 0.8 arcmin. At 5% contrast the threshold size grows by about √20, to roughly 3.5 arcmin (about 1 mrad). This approximately agrees with my recollection of Blackwell-type threshold data, though those figures are not checked. The 2 mm spot subtends 1 mrad at 2 mm / 0.001 ≈ 2 m."}
